shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The unit's onset frame, וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.11.11, byte tier), is the accent-variant twin of the frame opening the preceding verse, וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.11.10, byte tier) — identical to that verse at accent-stripped and skeleton tier, not at byte — and is itself byte-identical to the same formula's openers at oshb:Isa.10.20 and oshb:Isa.10.27 (sweep: 5 verses book-wide at byte tier); what discriminates this verse's action once that shared frame is set aside is the explicit agent shift that follows it, יוֹסִ֨יף אֲדֹנָ֤י שֵׁנִית֙ (oshb:Isa.11.11, byte tier), “It will happen in that day that the Lord will set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant that is left of his people from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.” (web:Isa.11.11). The unit closes on the second-exodus echo, “There will be a highway for the remnant that is left of his people from Assyria, like there was for Israel in the day that he came up out of the land of Egypt.” (web:Isa.11.16), at the chapter's own close.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the regathering promise into a Judah/Ephraim reconciliation unit and a separate highway unit is rejected because both remain governed by the same 'in that day' onset, with the narration staying third-person from onset to close.

shipped_row.device_notes: A petuchah mark closes the preceding unit at oshb:Isa.11.10; tier-3, single-witness, disclosed though the boundary is argued from the agent shift rather than the mark. Both this unit's onset and its close carry two of the remnant root's objects together, not one: the plain noun and, in the same clause, the survive-verb — אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִשָּׁאֵר֩ (oshb:Isa.11.11, byte tier) and לִשְׁאָ֣ר עַמּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִשָּׁאֵ֖ר (oshb:Isa.11.16, byte tier), that verb form reaching exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses), both inside this span; the closing verse echoes the opening one on this compound noun-plus-verb construction, not on the plain noun alone, distinct from the name-reactivating clauses argued earlier in this stretch (oshb:Isa.10.21-Isa.10.22).

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A formulaic onset restarts the Jesse figure as an ensign to the nations rather than continuing the peaceable-kingdom description: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא שֹׁ֣רֶשׁ יִשַׁ֗י (oshb:Isa.11.10, byte tier), “It will happen in that day that the nations will seek the root of Jesse, who stands as a banner of the peoples; and his resting place will be glorious.” (web:Isa.11.10). The following verse marks its own action as explicit repetition — יוֹסִ֨יף אֲדֹנָ֤י שֵׁנִית֙ (oshb:Isa.11.11, byte tier), “the Lord will set his hand again the second time” (web:Isa.11.11) — distinguishing that regathering act from the nations-seeking-the-root act named here, which argues for a boundary between them.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this verse back into the shoot-of-Jesse unit on the strength of the Jesse-name inclusio — יִשָׁ֑י (oshb:Isa.11.1, byte tier) against יִשַׁ֗י (oshb:Isa.11.10, byte tier), matching at word-bound consonantal-skeleton tier (sweep: 2 verses book-wide — the 22-verse bare-substring digit is a short-token trap, not the citable object) — is rejected because that echo is citation-grade against two tier-1 signals: the in-that-day discourse frame opening this verse where the preceding one carries none, and the explicit agent shift opening the next. A weaker rival folds this verse forward into the regathering oracle instead on the shared in-that-day frame, which fails equally to discriminate the seam since both sides of that seam carry it.
prev_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
prev_row.device_notes: A petuchah mark closes the preceding unit at oshb:Isa.11.9, and the same mark type falls again at this unit's own verse, oshb:Isa.11.10; both tier-3, single-witness, named and typed without ranking one paragraph-break type against the other, corroborating rather than driving the boundary already argued from the frame and the agent shift. The in-that-day frame opening this verse, וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.11.10, byte tier), also opens the immediately following verse, וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.11.11, byte tier) — identical at accent-stripped and skeleton tier, not at byte (byte tier: 6 verses book-wide; accent-stripped and skeleton tier: 13 verses book-wide); once a frame carried by both sides of the rear seam is set aside, what still carries that seam is the explicit agent shift the next verse opens with, not the formula. The banner image also recurs across the rear seam: עֹמֵד֙ לְנֵ֣ס עַמִּ֔ים (oshb:Isa.11.10, byte tier) is unique at every tier (sweep: 1 verse), and וְנָשָׂ֥א נֵס֙ לַגּוֹיִ֔ם (oshb:Isa.11.12, byte tier) reaches 2 verses at skeleton tier; the bare banner noun itself may not be swept for this claim — it is a short-token trap reaching 44 verses as a substring against 6 word-bound, the word-bound set not including this verse's own prefixed form. Whether this verse is better read as the closing coda of the preceding shoot-of-Jesse unit, as its own bridge, or as the opening of the regathering oracle that follows is not fully settled; the boundary drawn here is the held, honestly-medium_low position.

next_row.boundary_rationale: The unit opens the chapter-bounded thanksgiving hymn with its first strophe, וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.12.1, byte tier), “In that day you will say,” (web:Isa.12.1), and its own doubled divine name יָ֣הּ יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.12.2, byte tier), “for Yah, Yahweh, is my strength and song” (web:Isa.12.2). A second strophe opens with a distinct verb form, וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֞ם בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.12.4, byte tier), “In that day you will say,” (web:Isa.12.4); the two onsets are distinct at byte, accent-stripped and skeleton tier, and the two share the in-that-day core, which matches at accent-stripped and skeleton tier but not at byte, so the second strophe is read as continuing rather than opening a new addressee, and the unit closes at the chapter's own end, “for the Holy One of Israel is great among you!” (web:Isa.12.6).
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the hymn at its second 'you will say' onset into two separate rows is rejected because both strophes share the same speaker and doxological register within one chapter-bounded unit, even though the second strophe's plural verb turns to a wider addressee than the earlier strophe's singular.

next_row.device_notes: A petuchah mark closes this unit at its own final verse, oshb:Isa.12.6; tier-3, single-witness, disclosed though the close is already fixed by the frame boundary carried forward from the larger architecture. The twin 'in that day you will say' onsets at web:Isa.12.1 and web:Isa.12.4 share the same underlying in-that-day core even though the verb of speaking differs in number, both being second person, singular against plural; both strophes are kept inside one hymn rather than split, since speaker and register stay constant even where the addressed number widens. The closing title, קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Isa.12.6, byte tier), stands as the signature title object rather than resting on the English alone. A ketiv/qere note also sits at web:Isa.12.5 — single-witness, content not sliced here. The Yah-plus-tetragrammaton stack at web:Isa.12.2 is counted as its own short-form site (sweep: 3 verses book-wide), a count-object separate from the 394-verse tetragrammaton census. This unit spans the whole of chapter 12 (6 verses, the book's verse inventory), so confidence here is held at medium_low under the campaign's whole-chapter cap rather than lowered by any new defect in the boundary argument itself.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The unit opens with the compound chazah/ben-Amots superscription fused to the massa Bavel header — “The burden of Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz saw.” (web:Isa.13.1) — spliced from מַשָּׂ֖א בָּבֶ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה יְשַׁעְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן אָמֽוֹץ (oshb:Isa.13.1, byte tier), where the burden-word and the vision-word are fused in one clause rather than as a separate notice. The header is read as the hinge opening the massa series: it binds its target to the burden-noun in construct, מַשָּׂ֖א בָּבֶ֑ל (oshb:Isa.13.1, byte tier), rather than standing apart as a third stand-alone superscription row alongside Isa.1.1 and Isa.2.1. From web:Isa.13.2 the summons to muster nations for Yahweh's day, the darkened sky, and the terrified peoples run as one scene through web:Isa.13.16, before the span's close, where the first-person-suffixed presentative הִנְנִ֛י (oshb:Isa.13.17, byte tier) introduces a named agent; the distinctive feature at that turn is the first-person suffix on the presentative itself, since divine first person already runs within this span at אֲנִ֥י צִוֵּ֖יתִי (oshb:Isa.13.3, byte tier) and וּפָקַדְתִּ֤י (oshb:Isa.13.11, byte tier), and a bare presentative already stands at הִנֵּ֤ה יוֹם יְהוָה֙ בָּ֔א (oshb:Isa.13.9, byte tier).
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Setting Isa.13.1 apart as a third stand-alone superscription row alongside Isa.1.1 and Isa.2.1 was rejected because this header binds its target to the burden-noun in construct, מַשָּׂ֖א בָּבֶ֑ל (oshb:Isa.13.1, byte tier), where the other header attaches its target with a preposition after the patronymic, בֶּן אָמ֑וֹץ עַל יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָֽם (oshb:Isa.2.1, byte tier) — the relative clause common to both is byte-identical across all three headers and so cannot separate them.

next_row.boundary_rationale: A causal clause reorients the addressee from Babylon's fall to Jacob's restoration — “For Yahweh will have compassion on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land.” (web:Isa.14.1) — opening with the subordinating particle כִּי֩ (oshb:Isa.14.1, byte tier), whose clause is syntactically dependent on the announcement closing the preceding unit; the seam itself is carried not by that particle but by the participant shift into Jacob and Israel, יְרַחֵ֨ם יְהוָ֜ה אֶֽת יַעֲקֹ֗ב וּבָחַ֥ר עוֹד֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Isa.14.1, byte tier), which brings a fresh addressee in as the object of both verbs against the Babylon-palace subjects that close the preceding unit. The promise closes at web:Isa.14.2 with the nations' captivity reversed, before the temporal frame that reopens the unit toward the king-of-Babylon mashal at web:Isa.14.3.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Typing this couplet as an independent salvation_oracle was considered but set aside because the header governing this span (Isa.13.1) still stands and the addressee shift is argued from a causal clause, not from a fresh tier-1 frame of its own.

queue_items.claim: The seam's stated tier-1 warrant is recorded as an addressee shift, but the couplet and the verse closing the preceding unit carry no addressee at all - the shift is a participant/topic shift, and the signal key overstates it.
queue_items.grounds: oshb:Isa.14.1 and oshb:Isa.14.2 are third person throughout at byte tier: יְרַחֵ֨ם יְהוָ֜ה אֶֽת יַעֲקֹ֗ב and וְנִלְוָ֤ה הַגֵּר֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם (oshb:Isa.14.1, byte tier), וּלְקָח֣וּם עַמִּים֮ and וְרָד֖וּ בְּנֹגְשֵׂיהֶֽם (oshb:Isa.14.2, byte tier) - no second-person form and no vocative anywhere in the two verses, and oshb:Isa.13.22 closing the preceding unit is likewise third person. The rationale nevertheless says the shift brings a fresh addressee in as the object of both verbs (a verbal object is not an addressee), and observed_substrate_signals records oracle_frame.addressee_shift_restoration_promise. The ruled tier-1 inventory names addressee/scene shifts, vocatives and imperative onsets; the first actual addressee in this stretch is the second-person cluster one verse later at oshb:Isa.14.3 - וְהָיָ֗ה בְּי֨וֹם הָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ לְךָ֔ with מֵֽעָצְבְּךָ֖ וּמֵרָגְזֶ֑ךָ and verse-final אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֻבַּד בָּֽךְ (all oshb:Isa.14.3, byte tier) - which sits at the NEXT row's opening seam, not at this one. The row's own opening word is the backward-binding כִּי֩ (oshb:Isa.14.1, byte tier), which the rationale itself concedes is syntactically dependent on the preceding unit.

The promise closes at web:Isa.14.2 with the nations' captivity reversed, before the temporal frame that reopens the unit toward the king-of-Babylon mashal at web:Isa.14.3.

The near-time predication also brackets the whole Babylon burden across this same seam at skeleton tier (sweep: 8 verses book-wide): כִּ֥י קָר֖וֹב (oshb:Isa.13.6, byte tier) opens the day-of-Yahweh call and וְקָר֤וֹב לָבוֹא֙ (oshb:Isa.13.22, byte tier) closes the following unit's last line. queue_items.claim: The warrant binding the row's opening verse to the next one - and so placing the left edge at Isa.14.3 rather than Isa.14.4 - is a WEB sentence/punctuation fact, the exact tier-4 class barred as driver or corroboration.
queue_items.grounds: boundary_rationale states that the temporal clause at web:Isa.14.3 runs as one sentence into the frame verb at web:Isa.14.4. That one-sentence relation is a property of the WEB rendering alone - web:Isa.14.3 ends on a comma and the next verse opens with a subordinating conjunction in the WEB text - i.e. tier-4 metadata, never boundary evidence and never corroboration. The byte-tier fact that would carry the same continuity is never named: oshb:Isa.14.3 opens וְהָיָ֗ה בְּי֨וֹם הָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ לְךָ֔ (byte tier) and oshb:Isa.14.4 continues with the waw-consecutive perfect וְנָשָׂ֜אתָ (byte tier), the protasis-apodosis chain that makes the two verses one syntactic unit under the campaign's continuous-sentence rule. The row's only Hebrew splice is taken from oshb:Isa.14.4, the span's second verse. This is the only tier-4 vocabulary in any of the eight rows of this slice.
queue_items.proposed_change: Re-ground the continuity clause on the oshb:Isa.14.3|oshb:Isa.14.4 waw-consecutive chain (וְהָיָ֗ה בְּי֨וֹם הָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ לְךָ֔ ... וְנָשָׂ֜אתָ, byte tier) and drop the WEB sentence fact from the warrant. No span change proposed.

next_row.boundary_rationale: A divine-signature bracket opens and closes this couplet: Isa.14.22 reads “I will rise up against them,” says Yahweh of Armies, “and cut off from Babylon name and remnant, and son and son’s son,” says Yahweh. (web:Isa.14.22), opening וְקַמְתִּ֣י עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת (oshb:Isa.14.22, byte tier), and Isa.14.23 closes “I will also make it a possession for the porcupine, and pools of water. I will sweep it with the broom of destruction,” says Yahweh of Armies. (web:Isa.14.23), ending נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת (oshb:Isa.14.23, byte tier). Three signature tokens stand across these two verses rather than a simple repetition: the mid-verse נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת (oshb:Isa.14.22, byte tier) opens the judgment, the same verse closes with the bare-tetragrammaton stack נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.14.22, byte tier, no hosts-title), and Isa.14.23 itself ends with the hosts-title restored, נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת (oshb:Isa.14.23, byte tier). This postpositive signature chain marks a self-contained first-person judgment against Babylon's name and remnant, set off from the mashal that precedes it and from the oath-formula oracle that follows at web:Isa.14.24.

queue_items.claim: The row's left edge depends on reading the mid-verse burden-word at Isa.14.28 as pointing forward, and that directional claim is asserted flatly, with no byte ground and no disclosure of the standing backward-pointing construal that would place Isa.14.28 with the preceding oracle.
queue_items.grounds: boundary_rationale states that the burden-word sits mid-verse as a header reference inside the regnal dating frame, pointing forward to the burden this row's own span carries. The verse's own bytes end הָיָ֖ה הַמַּשָּׂ֥א הַזֶּֽה (oshb:Isa.14.28, byte tier) - an anaphoric-capable demonstrative that the row never engages - and nothing else in the verse fixes direction. strongest_rejected_alternative disposes only of the FORM question (mid-verse header reference vs the verse-initial header class), not the direction question, although the second-sentence slot reserved for a mandated rival disclosure is unused. The claim is load-bearing: on the backward construal Isa.14.28 closes the preceding unit and this row opens at Isa.14.29. The forward reading is well supported on other grounds the row does hold (inventory petuchah at Isa.14.27; the Philistia address opening at Isa.14.29), so the boundary is not shown wrong here - the warrant is.
